expectations.text: Recommends Expected Influence over Strength, or recommends both with Expected Influence as the primary index for this network
expectations.evidence: "report both, but prioritize Expected Influence" and the table row: "Mixed-valence affect network like yours | Expected Influence, report Strength too" and "Lead interpretation with EI"

expectations.text: Explains the substantive reason: Strength sums absolute edge weights and loses sign information, so nodes with large positive and large negative edges get inflated Strength scores that don't reflect their net influence
expectations.evidence: "Strength counts both as equal evidence of centrality — it sees a highly connected node" and "Strength inflates centrality estimates for nodes with many cross-valence connections" and the formula S_i = Σ |w_ij| vs EI_i = Σ w_ij explicitly showing the absolute value difference

expectations.text: Notes that negative edges between positive and negative affect items are structurally expected in an affect network, making sign information important
expectations.evidence: "Your 8-item affect network will almost certainly have negative edges — specifically between the PA and NA clusters (enthusiastic ↔ distressed, inspired ↔ upset, etc.). The two clusters will each have positive internal edges, with negative cross-valence edges bridging them."

expectations.text: Attributes Expected Influence to Robinaugh et al. (2016) OR makes the equivalent point that EI was developed specifically to handle networks with negative edges without the attribution
expectations.evidence: No attribution to Robinaugh et al. (2016) is given. The response explains why EI is preferred in contexts with negative edges, but never states that EI was developed specifically to address the problem of negative edges — only that it is preferred in such contexts.

expectations.text: Notes that for unipolar networks (where all edges are positive), Strength and Expected Influence are equivalent OR does not contradict this
expectations.evidence: Table row explicitly states: "All edges positive (e.g., psychopathology symptom net) | Strength (EI ≈ Strength anyway)"
